To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
activation of Wnt signaling is sufficient to induce tubule formation in kidney mesenchymes.
the canonical Wnt signaling pathway is required for nephron induction and differentiation in the metanephros.
activation of canonical (beta-catenin-dependent) Wnt pathway is both necessary and sufficient for nephron induction in metanephric kidney mesenchymes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of nephron induction in metanephric kidney mesenchymes and the role of Wnt signaling in nephrogenesis.
the mechanisms of epithelial differentiation in the embryonic kidney and the intracellular signaling events downstream of Wnt signaling in nephrogenesis.
the mechanisms of nephron formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Wnt signaling is a key pathway for nephrogenesis and that the intracellular mechanisms by means of which it mediates tubulogenesis and epithelial differentiation are now identified.
GSK3 inactivation and beta-catenin stabilization in kidney mesenchyme cells are sufficient to induce epithelial differentiation, and thus to induce nephrogenic competence.
GSK3 inhibition and stabilization of beta catenin are sufficient to induce nephrocytogenesis in isolated kidney mesengymes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Wnt signaling pathway is a key regulator of nephrogenesis.
the Wnt signaling pathway is required for the nephron induction.
the Wnt signaling is sufficient and necessary to induce nephron development in the embryonic kidney.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Wnt pathway is required for nephron induction in metanephric kidney mesenchymes.
Wnt signaling is sufficient to induce kidney mesenchyme differentiation and that the canonical Wnt pathway mediates this process.
GSK3 inhibition is sufficient to induce kidney development in the absence of ureteric bud and that the downstream mechanism of GSK3 inactivation is beta-catenin stabilization.
